options: To turn high volumes of staged, imported transaction data into real Receivables transactions without manual entry
To replace the need for transaction types
To merge duplicate customer records
To calculate customer credit limits
questions.explain: AutoInvoice scales billing for businesses that generate far more transactions than a team could key in manually, using an Imported transaction source.

questions.q: What are the three phases AutoInvoice runs every batch through, in order?
options: Transfer, validation, grouping
Validation, grouping, transfer
Grouping, transfer, validation
Completion, printing, closing
questions.explain: AutoInvoice first validates line-level data, then groups validated lines into transactions, then transfers them into the real Receivables tables.

questions.q: What happens to a line that fails AutoInvoice validation?
options: It is silently deleted
It is created as a transaction anyway, with a warning
It is moved to an interface errors table for review and resubmission after correction
It automatically becomes a chargeback
questions.explain: Failed records are preserved in an errors table, not lost or forced through, so they can be corrected and resubmitted.

questions.q: In the Northwind Fixtures Co. example, why did 3 of the 400 lines fail validation?
options: They exceeded the customer's credit limit
They used the wrong currency
They were duplicate transactions
They referenced a customer site that had been end-dated
questions.explain: The 3 failing lines referenced an end-dated customer site, which is exactly the kind of line-level issue the validation phase catches.

questions.q: What does the grouping phase of AutoInvoice do?
options: It combines validated lines into transaction headers according to a configured grouping rule, and validates header-level consistency
It deletes transactions that are too large
It calculates sales tax for every line
It assigns a collector to overdue accounts
questions.explain: Grouping takes validated lines and assembles them into one or more transaction headers based on rules about which lines belong together.
